blocks.text: The following pages outline acceptable combinations of medications for treatment of diabetes.
blocks.html: The following pages outline acceptable combinations of medications for treatment of diabetes.

blocks.text: PHARMACEUTICAL CONSIDERATIONS:
blocks.html: PHARMACEUTICAL CONSIDERATIONS:

blocks.text:
- Initial Certification/Clearance decision is made by the FAA. The AME must defer.
- Unlisted Medications: Consult AMCD or RFS.
- See below for acceptable medication combinations and required observation times.
blocks.html:
• Initial Certification/Clearance decision is made by the FAA. The AME must defer.
  • Unlisted Medications: Consult AMCD or RFS.
  • See below for acceptable medication combinations and required observation times.

blocks.text: - 1. Combination Medication: Count each component in a combination medication separately (e.g., rosiglitazone + metformin = 2 medications).
blocks.html: • 1. Combination Medication: Count each component in a combination medication separately (e.g., rosiglitazone + metformin = 2 medications).

blocks.text: - Combinations of up to 3 non-insulin medications are considered acceptable for routine treatment according to generally accepted standards of care for diabetes (American Diabetes Association, American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists). Follow up/recertification may be under the AASI program .
blocks.html: • Combinations of up to 3 non-insulin medications are considered acceptable for routine treatment according to generally accepted standards of care for diabetes (American Diabetes Association, American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists). Follow up/recertification may be under the AASI program .

blocks.text: - 4 or more medications may be considered on a case-by-case basis.
blocks.html: • 4 or more medications may be considered on a case-by-case basis.

blocks.text: - 2. Only ONE Medication allowed from each group (A–G).
blocks.html: • 2. Only ONE Medication allowed from each group (A–G).

blocks.text: - - - Insulin Exception: An insulin regimen containing multiple insulin types (e.g., short-acting [aspart] + long-acting [glargine]) counts as 1 medication.
blocks.html: • Insulin Exception: An insulin regimen containing multiple insulin types (e.g., short-acting [aspart] + long-acting [glargine]) counts as 1 medication.

blocks.text: - - - If using insulin (any type), see Medical Certification Using Insulin
blocks.html: • If using insulin (any type), see Medical Certification Using Insulin

blocks.text: - 3. Follow observation times on tables.
blocks.html: • 3. Follow observation times on tables.
